text:
chandra: quick Q — I'm landing the tf-module refactor for payments and need a sanity check on provider pinning + k8s serviceAccount -> secret path annotations. noticed the module now expects a provider source pinned to registry.example.com/infra/aws v1.2.0, but the root lockfile is still pointing at hash-based mirror entries. will that mismatch break consumers?

alex: it shouldn't break runtime if lockfile resolves, but plan/apply can fail if root module and child modules disagree on required provider constraints. best to align the module's required_providers block with the root provider alias used in the lockfile.

matt: can you paste the module snippet? also, are you changing the provider aliasing that we use for cross-account STS?

chandra: yep changing aliasing — snippet below. planning to set a strict version constraint so Dedicated infra gets stable kernel picks.
```
module "payments" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra-terraform/modules/payments.git?ref=v2-refactor"
  providers = {
    aws = aws.payments
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  alias  = "payments"
  region = var.payments_region
  version = "~> 4.30"
}
```

jen: two quick things — 1) if you tighten the version in the module but the root wants a slightly different constraint, running `terraform init -upgrade` will show conflicts. 2) for the secret path mapping, we added a k8s annotation pattern last quarter: `redwood.com/secret-path: "secrets/{{service}}/{{env}}"` — that needs the SA annotation set by the k8s manifest generator.

chandra: right — currently the deployment template uses the old annotation key `infra.redwood/secret` so I need to update the helm values. wondering if it's safe to change in one deploy or should we do a two-step rename?

alex: two-step safer — add the new annotation in parallel and keep old one for a release or two. consumers read the new key first and fall back. avoids hard fails during rollout. :+1:

matt: for provider pinning: if you want deterministic lockfiles across CI agents, we should pin to the mirror-based checksums in the root lockfile. I recommend bumping the module constraint to match root and then regenerating the lockfile from root CI (so the lockfile contains the correct checksum mapping).

chandra: makes sense. plan: 1) update module required_providers to use the same constraint as root (i'll open a PR), 2) update helm chart values to include both annotations, and 3) trigger root lockfile regen job. anyone object?

jen: no objections. one ask — can you add a short migration note in the PR body listing the clusters we need to watch (staging, production-eu)?

chandra: will do. matt, can you run the lockfile regen job once my module PR is merged? I don't have rights on the CI runner that writes to the monorepo lockfile.

matt: sure — ping me in the PR and I'll run it. also add a smoke test for the payments deploy that checks the annotation presence (helm test or a tiny curl to the pod metadata).

chandra: added to checklist. final q: any gotchas with provider aliasing + module-level providers that have different assume_role configurations? we rely on aws.payments to assume a payments role.

alex: make sure the provider alias block in the module doesn't redeclare shared config like region or endpoints if you want to inherit from root. better to pass the alias provider from root as you have in the snippet. module-level provider declarations are used only if the consumer doesn't pass them in.

tf-bot: reminder: after lockfile regen, run `make infra-lint` in CI to catch provider constraint drift.

chandra: thanks all — i'll open the module PR now and update the helm chart PR with dual annotations. will ping matt to run lockfile regen after merge.

alex: thanks — and optional: mention the rollout window in the PR for safety (low traffic window).

chandra: noted, will schedule canary during 0300-0500 UTC. :thumbsup:
